rituals.title: SPACED ECHO
rituals.mission: Repeat the same item two different ways and compare what sticks.
rituals.rule: One pair is massed; one pair is separated by distraction.
rituals.play: Repeat MOON twice back-to-back. Then say RIVER once, count 1–5, and say RIVER again. Wait five seconds and notice which word returns more readily.
rituals.twist: Do not rehearse either word during the final wait.
rituals.win: Spacing changes memory strength even though total repetitions are equal.
rituals.mind_bend: Identical material can leave different memory strength depending on spacing, exposing timing as part of encoding rather than a neutral container around it.

TWIST

WIN

MIND BEND

rituals.win: Temporal direction changes while elements remain the same.
rituals.mind_bend: A remembered sequence can be traversed backward, showing that mental replay order is manipulable even when the original event had only one direction.

rituals.title: FAST FORWARD
rituals.mission: Compress perceived duration by speed.
rituals.play: Run the familiar clip extremely fast until beginning and end almost touch.
rituals.win: The same sequence occupies far less subjective time.
rituals.mind_bend: Accelerating a repetitive clip changes its felt character without adding events, revealing speed as a separate parameter from narrative content.

rituals.title: FREEZE FRAME
rituals.mission: Stop motion without erasing image.
rituals.play: Let the clip run briefly, then freeze on an ordinary non-peak moment.
rituals.twist: keep it three beats then finish freeze frame.
rituals.win: Motion can stop while visual content remains.
rituals.mind_bend: A moving mental event is built from moments that can be isolated; freezing one frame separates a single state from the motion surrounding it.

rituals.title: MOTION TRAIL
rituals.mission: Leave a trail behind one moving image.
rituals.play: Run a short harmless mental motion. Let each previous position stay behind as a transparent ghost while the object keeps moving.
rituals.twist: Keep only the last four ghost positions.
rituals.win: The movie becomes a visible path of past positions instead of a single moving frame.
rituals.mind_bend: Visible traces of earlier positions turn motion into a stack of locations, revealing how the mind can integrate separate spatial states into one moving object.

rituals.win: The movie reduces to discrete change-events rather than continuous replay.

rituals.title: THOUGHT REBOUND TEST
rituals.mission: Test the rebound effect of permission instead of suppression.
rituals.play: For five seconds, intentionally allow the thought to be present as much as it wants, then stop inviting it.
rituals.twist: Do not push it out afterward.
rituals.win: You observe whether deliberate permission changes the thought's behaviour.
rituals.mind_bend: Inviting a mild recurring thought can change its persistence, revealing how resistance and suppression may help maintain the very return they are trying to prevent.

rituals.title: EVENT-BOUNDARY CUT

rituals.play: Recall a mild recent sequence and locate the first clear shift in place, goal or activity—such as leaving the car and entering the shop. Treat that shift as the event boundary.
rituals.twist: Do not replay details on both sides once the boundary is found.
rituals.win: Memory becomes segmented by event structure rather than by an imposed time window.
rituals.mind_bend: A remembered episode naturally breaks where goal, place or activity changes, revealing event boundaries as context shifts rather than arbitrary slices of clock time.

rituals.mind_bend: Tomorrow-you can be imagined as offering one concise sentence, revealing how a small shift in temporal perspective can compress what currently feels mentally crowded.

rituals.title: TEMPORAL DISCOUNT DUEL
rituals.mission: Find where waiting becomes worth it.
rituals.rule: Only reward size and delay may vary.
rituals.play: Choose between $20 today and $30 in one month. Then change the later delay to one week, then six months, and notice where your preference flips.
rituals.twist: Do not add risk or other reasons.
rituals.win: Time delay reveals its own influence on value.
rituals.mind_bend: Preference can flip solely because reward delay changes, uncovering how the mind discounts future value even when the rewards themselves remain otherwise comparable.

rituals.title: TOPOLOGICAL ORDER
rituals.mission: Put dependent steps into a legal sequence.
rituals.rule: A step may appear only after all of its prerequisites.
rituals.play: Use: A has no prerequisite; B requires A; C requires A; D requires both B and C. Produce one valid order for A, B, C, D.
rituals.twist: B and C may swap places because neither depends on the other.
rituals.win: A legal sequence emerges from dependency structure rather than preference.
rituals.mind_bend: Prerequisites can force a valid action order without saying which task matters most, separating dependency structure from importance ranking.

rituals.win: The future gains flexibility without becoming fantasy.
rituals.mind_bend: A future can contain one realistic advantage without becoming a perfect-outcome fantasy, showing that optimism can be specific rather than totalising.

rituals.title: ROLE-NAME MEMORY
rituals.mission: Give the same word two roles and see which one memory remembers better.
rituals.rule: The label stays identical; only its role changes.
rituals.play: Imagine one person introduced as 'Baker'—a surname. Imagine another described as 'a baker'—the profession. After five seconds, recall everything you can about each.
rituals.twist: Do not add extra facts deliberately.
rituals.win: Meaningful role context changes what the same verbal label makes memorable.
rituals.mind_bend: The richer trace comes from the role assigned during encoding, proving that identical material can inherit different memory cues from its assigned meaning.

rituals.title: SOURCE FAMILY TREE
rituals.mission: Count independent evidence, not repeated copies.
rituals.rule: Two reports derived from one original source count as one evidence branch.
rituals.play: Imagine Article A cites Report X, Article B also cites Report X, and Article C cites Study Y. Draw the source tree mentally and count independent roots.
rituals.twist: Do not count publication titles as separate evidence if they share a root.
rituals.win: Three apparent sources collapse into two independent evidence origins.
rituals.mind_bend: Evidence has ancestry: many downstream reports still count as one branch when they inherit the same original source, revealing redundancy hidden by publication count.

rituals.title: TEACH-BACK CHECK
rituals.mission: Prove you understood the answer by teaching it back.
rituals.rule: Use your own wording without adding new information.
rituals.play: Take a simple answer such as 'The appointment moved from 2pm to 3pm.' Restate it from memory using different wording, then compare against the original fact.
rituals.twist: Any changed time, condition or qualifier counts as a comprehension error.
rituals.win: Understanding is checked through accurate reconstruction rather than repeated questioning.
rituals.mind_bend: Restating information in your own words can expose a changed time, condition or qualifier, revealing comprehension as something testable beyond the feeling of understanding.

rituals.title: UNCERTAINTY LANGUAGE
rituals.mission: Make language match knowledge.
rituals.play: Convert 'definitely/never/must' to 'maybe/likely/unlikely/unknown' only if more accurate.
rituals.win: Wording becomes calibrated to evidence.
rituals.mind_bend: Replacing absolute certainty words with probability language can change a sentence’s claim without positive spin, revealing how grammar can overstate confidence beyond the evidence.

rituals.title: NOT-KNOWING POSTURE
rituals.mission: Pair uncertainty with ordinary behavior.
rituals.play: Sit/stand normally, hands doing nothing special, while holding the words 'not known yet' for five seconds.
rituals.win: Not knowing coexists with ordinary posture/action.
rituals.mind_bend: Uncertainty does not prescribe a body posture; remaining physically neutral while the answer stays open separates not-knowing from bodily bracing.

rituals.title: UNCERTAINTY QUOTA
rituals.mission: Reserve space for unknowns.
rituals.play: When planning, leave one slot marked TBD instead of forcing a guess.
rituals.win: Plans can function while containing uncertainty.
rituals.mind_bend: A plan can intentionally contain one unresolved item and still proceed through known steps, proving that incomplete information need not block action.

WIN
Plans can function while containing uncertainty.

MIND BEND

rituals.title: MAX-INFO QUESTION
rituals.mission: Ask the question that cuts uncertainty closest to half.
rituals.play: Imagine eight possible cards numbered 1–8. Compare asking 'Is it even?' with 'Is it greater than 7?' Decide which question would eliminate more possibilities regardless of the answer.
rituals.twist: Judge the split, not which answer you hope for.
rituals.win: A well-chosen question reduces uncertainty by dividing possibilities efficiently.
rituals.mind_bend: A yes-no question removes the most uncertainty when it divides possibilities as evenly as possible, making information gain a feature of the split—not of the answer you hope for.

rituals.title: REALITY PARTNER
rituals.mission: Use external verification for destabilizing uncertainty.
rituals.rule: Do not act on frightening interpretation alone.
rituals.play: Prepare one concrete question about what is happening and verify it with someone you trust or a clinician.
rituals.win: A real-world verification channel replaces solitary certainty loops.
rituals.mind_bend: A frightening interpretation that is hard to verify belongs in shared reality with another person, revealing external checking as a safety tool when solitary certainty is unreliable.
rituals.support_first: If you feel unsafe, disconnected from shared reality, unable to verify frightening experiences, at risk of harming yourself or someone else, or may be having a medical emergency, use real-world human/medical support rather than relying on an inward game.

rituals.title: THOUGHT TRANSFORMATION TRACE
rituals.mission: Track transformation, not novelty.
rituals.play: When a recurring thought returns, compare whether its form changed—word to image, longer to shorter, question to statement, etc.
rituals.win: Recurrence can be studied as transformation rather than same/new classification.
rituals.mind_bend: A recurring thought may return with changed structure despite feeling like ‘the same thought again’, revealing repetition as capable of mutation between appearances.

rituals.title: UNCERTAINTY TWO-MODE
rituals.mission: Use solvability as mode selector.
rituals.rule: One decision: knowable now or not.
rituals.play: Ask whether the missing information can be obtained now. If yes, choose one information action; if no, choose one present behaviour that doesn't require it.
rituals.win: Uncertainty routes into different behavior based on obtainability.
rituals.mind_bend: Uncertainty calls for problem solving when information is obtainable and acceptance when it is not, revealing the cost of using the wrong mental mode for the situation.
